parts.text: In this experiment, you will use a pendulum to determine a value for the acceleration of free fall g . Carry out the following instructions, referring to Figs. 1.1 and 1.2. Fig. 1.1 Fig. 1.2 A pendulum has been set up for you as shown in Fig. 1.1.

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text:
Either suitable use of a horizontal straight edge
Or holding rule close to pendulum
Or line of sight perpendicular to rule

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Displace the pendulum bob slightly and release it so that it swings. Fig. 1.2 shows one complete oscillation of the pendulum.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the period T of the pendulum. The period is the time for one complete oscillation. T = ...........................................................[2]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Measuring the time for a large number of oscillations, rather than for 1 oscillation, gives a more accurate value for T . Suggest one practical reason why measuring the time for 200 oscillations, rather than 20 oscillations, may not be suitable. ........................................................................................................................................... .......................................................................................................................................[1]

ms.label: 1(b)(iii)
ms.text: More likely to miscount/pendulum may stop swinging

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the acceleration of free fall g using the equation g = 4 π 2 l T 2 . Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. g = ................................................. m / s 2 [2]

ms.label: 1(c)(ii)
ms.text:
g between 9 and 11 from correct T and working
2 or 3 significant figures

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) A student checks the value of the acceleration of free fall g in a text book. The value in the book is 9.8 m / s 2 .

ms.label: 1(d)(i)
ms.text:
Explanation of cause of inaccuracy in measurement of t or l.
e.g. student did not react quickly enough when starting/stopping stopwatch OR difficulty in
measuring accurately to centre of bob

ms.label: 1(d)(ii)
ms.text:
Any two from:
Use different length(s)
Repeat timing
Use of a fiducial mark
Increased number of oscillations
2
Plot a graph using length and time or time
